status: Owned-stock design options; no substitutions promoted
recommendation: Develop a through-hole variant using owned M27C322-100F1 for the ALU, M27C1024-10F1 for the control word, UM61512AK-15 for SRAM and W27C512-45Z for program ROM. All logic and memory must use DIP packages; SOIC is excluded. Reassess the mux/buffer fabric against available HCT245, HCT574 and HCT191 stock and one HCT157; more muxes can be obtained if verification shows a need.

parts.assessment: Exact match to the existing AL1 ROM timing model
parts.detail: ST 2M x16, 100 ns, windowed FDIP42W; multiple devices owned. Verification/alu-parts.json already models this exact part with 5 ns output hold and a 100 pF timing load. Replacing AL2's eight-flash array could remove its bank mux/address-buffer overhead. The AL1 route still needs a DIP-only supporting circuit and integrated FD1 verification. Programmer support remains to be checked.

ST 64K x16, 100 ns (-10), windowed FDIP40W (F), commercial temperature grade (1). Its organization matches the 65,536-word control store. One device could replace the two byte-wide control ROMs after controller pinout, footprint and timing-model changes. Verify the 100 ns access, enable/hold limits and loading in the integrated controller. Programmer support remains to be checked.

parts.assessment: Yes: suitable SRAM capacity and a promising faster owned candidate
parts.detail: 64K x8, 15 ns; the current AS6C1008 design grounds A16, so its extra capacity is unused. UMC specifies the K part as skinny DIP-32, unlike the current wide DIP-32 footprint. UMC pins 1 and 2 are NC; current AS6C1008 pin 2 is grounded A16. Use an exact symbol/footprint and revised timing/load model. Recommended DC supply is 4.75..5.25 V; read load 30 pF, high-Z timing test 5 pF, operating current up to 160 mA. Owned SRAM does not remove the separate turnaround qualification gap.

parts.assessment: Yes: strong program-ROM candidate; also usable as a control-ROM byte lane
parts.detail: 64K x8, 45 ns, lead-free 28-pin 600-mil DIP. Read-mode pin assignment matches the current 27C512-style ROM connections. One can cover the program-ROM role; two could cover the control ROM if that architecture is retained. The 45 ns rating uses 30 pF, read supply 4.75..5.25 V, and address-change output hold is 0 ns rather than the current AT27C512R model's 7 ns. Electrical erase/programming needs the correct programmer algorithm and elevated voltages (14 V erase / 12 V program); it is not a 5 V in-circuit byte-write EEPROM.

parts.assessment: DIP selected for the two retained operand-register functions
parts.detail: DL1 replaces the two reference CD74HCT377M96 SOIC parts with CD74HCT377E DIP parts. User-owned DIP HCT377 stock can fill this function after exact manufacturer/suffix and timing matching. The package selection does not qualify every vendor's HCT377.

parts.assessment: Design around the plentiful stock where the electrical role permits
parts.detail: A 245 can serve as an eight-bit unidirectional non-inverting buffer with DIR fixed, but has a different pin map and one common OE instead of the 244's two group enables. HCT cannot inherit AHCT propagation/drive limits, especially on clock and high-fanout paths. A 245 does not directly replace a 157 mux; using tri-state drivers as selection requires explicit non-overlap control and timing verification.

parts.assessment: Scarcer DIP stock; logic family still unknown
parts.detail: User reported fewer 244 devices than 74HCT245. Manufacturer, family and count remain unknown. The current 68 AHCT244 count belongs to the reference FD1 architecture; assess HCT245 buffer alternatives per electrical role.

parts.assessment: One DIP mux owned; more obtainable if needed
parts.detail: Family and quantity are confirmed. Exact manufacturer/suffix remain unknown. HCT157 timing must be modelled separately from AHCT157. The reference 84 AHCT157 count is not a purchasing requirement for the owned-DIP variant; determine the requirement after redesign and verification.

parts.assessment: Reuse in existing 574 roles; redesign needed to replace 175 registers
parts.detail: Five HCT574s are already in the reference candidate. A 574 lacks asynchronous clear, complementary outputs and clock enable; OE only controls outputs. All 48 reference AC175 positions use reset and three use complementary outputs. Reusing 574s for those registers therefore requires new reset/write behaviour and verification. DL1 uses pin-compatible CD74ACT175E DIP devices for that conversion. DIP ownership is confirmed; manufacturer/suffix and counts remain unknown.

parts.assessment: Useful stack/address-counter option requiring architectural work
parts.detail: This is a 4-bit up/down counter, relevant to the original stack/address roles. Current SP1/MA1 use adders, staging registers and muxes. Reusing 191s requires reviewing cascade, parallel-load, output timing and reset behaviour; it is not a pin-for-pin substitution for that architecture.

parts.assessment: DIP selected for PC and sequencer counters
parts.detail: DL1 replaces the five reference SOIC counters (four PC, one sequencer) with CD74HCT161E DIP devices. User-owned DIP HCT161 stock can fill this function after exact manufacturer/suffix and timing matching.

parts.assessment: Owned through-hole reset supervisor; existing supply-coverage gap remains
parts.detail: This exact TO-92 part already appears in the reset design. Existing DS11187F evidence gives a 4.25/4.375/4.50 V min/typ/max trip range and a 150/350/700 ms release delay. Release timing starts at threshold crossing, which may precede reaching the machine's 4.75 V valid-supply floor. Brownout assertion has only a typical delay in the cited table. Ownership resolves sourcing, while slow-ramp/startup, brownout and receiver recovery/removal still need qualification.

needed_from_user: Manufacturer and full suffixes for generic logic, plus the 244 logic family
Approximate counts except the confirmed single 74HCT157
EPROM programmer model and available adapters
scope: Inventory recording and datasheet-based suitability review only. No new simulation, physical qualification, normal-source change or revised purchase quantity.
